result.topic_en: Euler lists the polynomial equations between q and p for successive values of m, for even and odd m, and then for the case n = 3, before announcing a general form of these equations.
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 173
Primo pro valoribus paribus
$m=2;\ q^2-q^3=\tfrac{1}{2}p^4$
$m=4;\ q^2-q^3+q^4-q^5=\tfrac{1}{2}p^6$
$m=6;\ q^2-q^3+q^4-q^5+q^6-q^7=\tfrac{1}{2}p^8$
$m=8;\ q^2-q^3+q^4-q^5+q^6-q^7+q^8-q^9=\tfrac{1}{2}p^{10}$
etc.
Deinde pro valoribus imparibus:
$m=1;\ q^2=2p^2$ [?]
$m=3;\ 3q^2+q^3-3q^4=3p^5$
$m=5;\ 5q^2-q^3-q^4+3q^5-5q^6=4p^7$
$m=7;\ 7q^2-3q^3+q^4+3q^5-3q^6+5q^7-7q^8=5p^9$ [?]
$m=9;\ 9q^2-5q^3+3q^4-q^5-q^6+3q^7-5q^8+7q^9-9q^{10}=6p^{11}$
etc.
III. Si ponamus $n=3$ ſinguli caſus commodius perpenduntur, ſuntque primo pro $m$ numero impari
$m=1;\ q^2+q^3=3p^4$
$m=3;\ 6q^2+6q^3+3q^4-6q^5=7p^6$
$m=5;\ 15q^2-5q^3+6q^4-7q^5+10q^6-15q^7=13p^8$
$m=7;\ 28q^2-14q^3+13q^4-12q^5+13q^6-16q^7+21q^8-28q^9=21p^{10}$
etc.
pro ordinibus vero imparibus:
$m=2;\ 3q^2+q^3-3q^4=3p^5$
$m=4;\ 10q^2-2q^3-2q^4+6q^5-10q^6=8p^7$
$m=6;\ 21q^2-9q^3+3q^4+3q^5-9q^6+15q^7-21q^8=15p^9$
$m=8;\ 36q^2-20q^3+12q^4-4q^5-4q^6+12q^7-20q^8+28q^9-36q^{10}=24p^{11}$
etc.
hic pro vtroque ordine forma aequationis in genere expreſſa ita ſe habebit:
Y 3 ſi
